message: Clarify whether this behavior is mandatory ('shall') or optional.
poor: The system should send an email when a session changes.
improved: The system shall send an email notification when session attendance is amended.

message: Specify a measurable response or completion threshold.
poor: Staff shall quickly update session attendance.
improved: The system shall complete session attendance updates within 500ms under 99th percentile load.

message: Define the observable quality and how it will be evaluated.
poor: The session editor must be easy to use.
improved: First-time program staff shall complete an attendance amendment in under 2 minutes without external assistance during trial testing.

message: Define the security invariant, authentication role, or encryption requirement explicitly.
poor: Attendance records must be stored securely.
improved: Attendance audit history shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 and restricted to authorized Program Administrators.

message: Specify concrete throughput or capacity bounds.
poor: The reporting system must be scalable.
improved: The reporting job shall process up to 50,000 session records within a 15-minute maintenance window.

message: Check for boundary conditions, locked states, or exception paths.
poor: All completed sessions can be edited at any time.
improved: Completed sessions may be edited while the reporting period remains open.

message: Specify the exact system role or permission tier.
poor: Staff shall receive session reports.
improved: The session-management system shall deliver monthly reports to users with the Program Administrator role.

message: This statement contains multiple conjunctions. Check if it combines several distinct requirements.
poor: The system shall update attendance and notify volunteers and regenerate reports.
improved: Split into 3 distinct atomic requirements: 1. Update attendance, 2. Notify volunteers, 3. Regenerate reports.

message: Replace ambiguous pronouns with explicit noun phrases.
poor: When the report is generated, it shall be sent to them.
improved: When the report is generated, the system shall email the report to Program Administrators.

message: Identify who or what performs the action (use active voice).
poor: An audit log shall be created.
improved: The session-management service shall record an entry in the audit log.

message: Consider adding an explicit trigger or state condition (EARS syntax).
poor: The system permits attendance edits.
improved: WHEN an authorized administrator requests an edit, the system shall permit attendance updates.

message: Check if the positive required alternative or failure response is defined.
poor: Users shall not edit completed sessions.
improved: When a non-administrator attempts to edit a completed session, the system shall reject the request and display an access-denied message.

message: Verify if naming this technology is a mandatory constraint or a premature design decision.
poor: The system shall store attendance in a Postgres database.
improved: The system shall persist attendance records in an append-only relational store.

message: Replace qualitative descriptors with exact numerical boundaries.
poor: Staff shall be notified of large attendance changes.
improved: Staff shall be notified when attendance figures change by more than 15% after initial publishing.

message: Define system behavior when the operation fails or input is invalid.
poor: The system shall save attendance corrections.
improved: The system shall save attendance corrections; if network connectivity fails, the change shall be queued locally for auto-retry.

message: Ensure this domain-specific term is defined in the project glossary.
poor: Staff can update a completed session.
improved: Verify definition of 'completed session' in project domain glossary.

message: Focus on the required capability or policy rather than specific UI widgets.
poor: Add an edit button to the session screen.
improved: The session interface shall provide an attendance modification action for authorized roles.

message: Specify which exact system module, service, or interface component.
poor: The system shall process requests.
improved: The Session Management Service shall process attendance change requests.

message: Define audit logging and data retention requirements for saved records.
poor: Save attendance corrections.
improved: Save attendance corrections in an append-only audit trail preserving prior values for 7 years.

message: Specify permission authorization rules for state-modifying actions.
poor: Allow attendance to be edited.
improved: The system shall permit users with the Program Administrator role to amend attendance.
